title: Deviled eggs
summary: Hard-boiled egg halves filled with a tangy yolk, mayonnaise and mustard mixture and dusted with paprika.
steps: Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water by 2.5 cm (1 in) and bring to a boil. Cover, take off the heat and leave 11 minutes.
Move the eggs to a bowl of iced water for 15 minutes, then peel under running water.
Halve the eggs lengthwise and pop the yolks into a bowl. Mash with a fork until fine, then stir in the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, salt, pepper and hot sauce until smooth.
Spoon or pipe the filling into the whites. Dust with paprika and scatter with chives. Serve within a few hours, kept chilled.
tips: Eggs a week or so old peel more cleanly than very fresh ones.

origin.history: Boiled eggs served with spiced sauces were eaten in ancient Rome, and recipes for stuffed eggs with the yolk mixed with seasonings appear in medieval cookbooks, including one from 13th-century Andalusia. The word 'devilled', for food made hot with mustard or pepper, appears in English in the late 1700s, and in the United States 'deviled eggs' became a party and picnic staple in the twentieth century.
